study: The world of Jesus & the apostles
status: implemented and verified locally; not deployed

editorial.scope: Sole approved C page, gold palette from B; no comparison pill or duplicate pages.
editorial.sourcePolicy: Josephus-specific material excluded from general study. Existing research archives preserved.
editorial.art: Original CSS relationship diagrams; no external images or borrowed measured plans. Textual excerpts from local public-domain WEB.

intellectualSequence: Orient to unequal survival of evidence and regional government.
Trace work, synagogue and pilgrimage across Galilee and Judaea without treating Judaism as uniform.
Move through provincial government and urban assemblies.
Separate Paul’s complaint from architectural and scheduling hypotheses.
Compare Ephesian literary and inscribed voices without collapsing their chronology.
Return to travel, change over time and the evolution of scholarly questions.

migdal.title: Avshalom-Gorni & Najar · Migdal (2013)
migdal.access: Excavation report read, especially Area D and its coin contexts. Historical narrative outside the archaeological observations is not used.

migdal2026.title: Tzin & Najar · Migdal Junction (2026)
migdal2026.access: Excavation description, Areas A3–A4 and B3, and pottery discussion read. No identification of its public building as a synagogue is assumed.

talgam.title: Talgam, Avshalom-Gorni & Najar · From the Magdala Stone to the Syriac Bema (2025)
talgam.access: University publication record and publisher description reviewed. Full book not read; its proposed liturgical connections are further research, not established conclusions here.

horrell.title: David G. Horrell · Domestic Space and Christian Meetings at Corinth (2004)
horrell.access: Publisher abstract and visible notes read, not the full article. Abstract supports the critique of the default villa model and the proposed comparison with buildings east of Corinth’s theatre.

theissen.title: Gerd Theissen · Social Conflicts in the Corinthian Community (2003)
theissen.access: Abstract and visible notes read, not the full article. Identifies the debate with J. J. Meggitt’s Paul, Poverty and Survival (1998); Meggitt’s book was located through this reference, not read.

meeks.title: Wayne A. Meeks · The First Urban Christians (1983; second edition 2003)
meeks.access: Yale publisher description reviewed, not the full book. Used to orient further reading in the social history of Pauline groups.

salutaris.title: I.Ephesos 27 · Salutaris’s endowment, 104 CE
salutaris.access: THEATRUM’s German translation after H. Wankel, I.Ephesos Ia (1979), no. 27: opening decree and sections 22–90, 117–132 read. Parentheses mark restorations in the edition. English descriptions here are paraphrases, not a new critical translation.

myles.title: Robert J. Myles · Fishing for Entrepreneurs? (2019)
myles.access: Author’s online chapter, opening argument and methodological discussion read. Only the critique of modern entrepreneurial categories is used; source-dependent historical reconstructions elsewhere in the essay are excluded.

claims.claim: A coin dated 43 CE was found in the reading-room mosaic foundation.
claims.inference: If undisturbed, this gives a terminus post quem for laying that floor, not the founding date of the whole building.

claims.claim: An 80 CE coin is reported on the ceiling collapse.
claims.limit: Position on collapse is not a sealed find under collapse. No collapse year inferred.

claims.claim: Report distinguishes construction phases and describes the latest preserved phase.
claims.limit: Do not combine every architectural element into a simultaneous first-century scene.

claims.claim: 2026 report extends settlement west and records a public building with bench, plaster and floors whose boundaries are unclear; gathering function is suggested.
claims.limit: Not identified here as a synagogue. Public-building description alone insufficient.

claims.claim: Migdal Temple imagery and Theodotos dedication support discussing local assembly and Temple connections without a replacement model.
claims.limit: No universal service order or exact stone function reconstructed; fictional dialogue excluded.

claims.claim: Paul reports division, unequal eating and shame, and commands waiting.
claims.limit: Pastoral intervention, not neutral census; obedience unknown. Quoted fragments verified against data/plain/web/1CO.json.

claims.claim: Separate rooms and different arrival times are independently switchable possibilities.
claims.limit: No identified meeting house, number of participants, work schedule or causal certainty. Switching changes assumptions, not textual evidence.

claims.claim: Horrell challenges conventional villa model and proposes comparison with buildings east of theatre.
claims.limit: Full article not read. Alternative building is not identified as Paul’s assembly.

claims.claim: Theissen’s 2003 reply to Meggitt defends social interpretation of Corinthian conflicts.
claims.limit: No full reconstruction of either scholar’s economic model claimed; Meggitt book located, not read.

claims.claim: Romans 16 names women in Pauline networks; Philemon 10–16 raises Onesimus and slavery.
claims.limit: Neither identifies who prepared Corinth’s meal or which people went hungry there.

claims.claim: 104 CE endowment links Salutaris, Artemis images, theatre, civic bodies and provincial authorisation.
claims.limit: Later than Acts19 narrated events; restorations present in edition; programme not observation of every performance. No riot corroboration or exact route map.

claims.claim: Acts19 links craft income, Artemis honour, crowd and appeal to civic procedure.
claims.limit: Literary account; no independent verification of speeches; narrated 50sCE not asserted composition date.

claims.claim: Myles critiques entrepreneurial categories; Hakola2023 challenges uniformly negative pictures.
claims.limit: Myles2019 is not a response to Hakola2023. Only methodological critique used; no uniform prosperity or subsistence conclusion.

claims.claim: Mark1:20 mentions hired servants with Zebedee.
claims.limit: Not net income, debt balance, class census or proof of all fishers’ circumstances.

stratigraphicContexts.label: On the collapsed ceiling
stratigraphicContexts.observation: The report places this coin on the ceiling collapse.
stratigraphicContexts.inference: Its position associates it with material above the fallen ceiling. It does not, by itself, date the moment the roof fell. A coin can be lost long after it was minted.
stratigraphicContexts.excludes: “The synagogue was destroyed in 80 CE.” That converts a coin’s date into an event date without establishing the deposition history.

stratigraphicContexts.label: The mosaic floor
stratigraphicContexts.observation: The mosaic belongs to a sequence of alterations, not the building’s entire lifetime.
stratigraphicContexts.inference: A date for this floor cannot simply be assigned to every wall, earlier room or later use. Archaeologists date contexts and phases before reconstructing a building’s history.
stratigraphicContexts.excludes: “Every feature shown here existed at the same time.” A composite plan can quietly combine successive arrangements.

stratigraphicContexts.label: In the mosaic foundation
stratigraphicContexts.observation: A coin dated 43 CE was recovered in the reading-room mosaic’s foundation.
stratigraphicContexts.inference: If the context is undisturbed, the floor was laid no earlier than the coin’s issue. Archaeologists call this a terminus post quem: a date after which an event can occur. It is a lower bound, not an exact construction year.
stratigraphicContexts.excludes: “The whole synagogue was founded in 43 CE.” Neither the building’s first use nor the floor’s exact year follows from this coin alone.

annotatedPassage.quote: I hear that divisions exist among you, and I partly believe it.
annotatedPassage.title: A report filtered through a letter
annotatedPassage.note: Paul is responding to information and evaluating it. We hear his intervention, not a transcript from every participant. The recipients’ own explanations do not survive in this passage.

annotatedPassage.quote: One is hungry, and another is drunken.
annotatedPassage.title: An unequal meal is the firm starting point
annotatedPassage.note: The contrast concerns access to food and drink within a gathering. It warrants asking about resources and conduct. It supplies neither a membership census nor the dimensions of a dining room.

annotatedPassage.quote: put them to shame who don’t have enough
annotatedPassage.title: Food has become a question of dignity
annotatedPassage.note: Paul connects material lack with humiliation. Calling the gathering a household does not make it egalitarian. But the verse does not identify each participant’s income, occupation or legal status.

annotatedPassage.quote: when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
annotatedPassage.title: An instruction is not an observed outcome
annotatedPassage.note: The remedy addresses how they gather. It makes timing worth investigating, without proving a complete schedule of work and arrival. Paul’s command does not tell us whether the community obeyed.

researchGaps: Full Horrell2004 and Theissen2003 articles not accessed; arguments limited to abstracts and visible notes.
Meeks1983/2003 and Talgam et al2025 full books not read. Meggitt1998 located through Theissen, not read. They are marked as deeper reading.
No fresh critical Greek edition collation of I.Ephesos27; German translated and restored text examined, paraphrased without silently treating restorations as intact words.
Migdal2013 is preliminary; new2026 report concerns other excavation contexts. Publication development does not silently resolve exact function of stone or chronology of every phase.
No population, household-income, attendance or transport-duration dataset adequate for numerical reconstruction. Diagrams carry no such quantities.
Evidence privileges literate correspondents, civic donors and surviving buildings; enslaved labour and many women’s own voices remain asymmetrically represented.
Existing dossier access gaps for Adams, Hakola, Rathmayr, ORBIS and indexed institutional records remain in force.
